summary: K. Sambasiva Sastri was an Indologist. He served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library from around 1925 to 1935, succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri.
K. Srinivasan is an Indologist. He was a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and held a post at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

K. T. S. Sarao is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at DAV College, Panjab University, the University of Delhi, and the University of Cambridge under Raymond Allchin and Kenneth Roy Norman, later becoming professor at Delhi in 1995.
K. V. Puttappa was a linguistics scholar. He was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1924–1929), and the University of Mysore (~1927–1929).

K. V. Raman was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. Educated at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, he worked at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1957–1976) and the University of Madras.

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987), and Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian. Around 1935 to 1940, he served as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College.

K. V. Sarma was an Indologist and historian. Educated at University College Thiruvananthapuram and the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri, he held posts at the Oriental Research Institute, University of Madras, Panjab University, and the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute.

K. Venkata Ramanan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, at Harvard-Yenching Institute, and at Visva-Bharati University under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, where he also taught.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist. He studied under Kaitei Hayama, at Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō, and earned a doctorate at the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann, later holding professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities.

Kaiten Nukariya was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Ryodo Nukariya and at Komazawa and Keio universities. He lectured at Harvard University (~1913–1915) and served as professor and first president of Komazawa University.
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kakichi Kadowaki was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952) and under Sogen Omori, later holding a post at Sophia University from around 1970 to 1996.

Kakushō Ujiie was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He conducted research study at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970) and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

Kali Kinkar Datta was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute as Honorary Director (attested 1959–1966) and Joint Director (attested 1987), and was Vice-Chancellor of Patna University (attested 1973).

Kalidas Nag was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later taught (~1923–1955), and served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1942–1946).
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist. She completed doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani and held a post at the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology.

Kalu Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under Khakyab Dorje, Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, and Lama Norbu Dondrup. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung and abbot at Changchub Choeling.

Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
